title: The Hollywood Left and the Blacklist: A Chat With the Curator of Locarno’s Timely Retrospective for the Age of Trump & Co.
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 30, 2026 10:30pm 'A King in New York' Courtesy of Roy Export SAS The retrospective at this year’s Locarno Film Festival feels particularly timely, maybe even scarily so. Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist promises to put the spotlight on “one of the most turbulent and politically charged periods in the history of American cinema,” including the “Red Scare” and the infamous Hollywood blacklist of the McCarthy era. After all, during the period from 1947 to the early 1960s, Hollywood professionals suspected of communist ties faced a crackdown. The Swiss festival’s cinematic look back will provide “a complex portrait of an era in which creatives were confronted by unprecedented abuse of state and industry power and which they met, courageously, with fierce artistic resistance,” Locarno highlighted. Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist will “re-examine this repressive yet defiantly creative era, which mirrors the political attacks on free speech and artistic freedom seen again today.” Related Stories Movies 'Pachinko' Star Kim Minha to Host Busan Film Festival's Opening Ceremony Business Europe to Boycott World Cup in FIFA Protest Produced in partnership with the Cinémathèque Suisse and with the support of UCLA Film & Television Archive, the Locarno retrospective was once again curated by Ehsan Khoshbakht . He has compiled a program of more than 50 films – fiction, documentaries, and shorts – and newsreels featuring such directors, writers, and stars as John Garfield, Joseph Losey, Dalton Trumbo , Dorothy Parker, Richard Wright, and Charlie Chaplin . It will explore various works to shine a spotlight on a time of polarized politics, allegations of communist infiltration of Hollywood in the Cold War, and the Hollywood blacklist that upended careers and forced artists to adopt pseudonyms or go into exile overseas. Among the films featured in the retrospective are the likes of Lewis Milestone’s The North Star (1943), None But the Lonely Heart (1944), directed by Clifford Odets, Crossfire (1947) from director Edward Dmytryk, Bernard Vorhaus’ Amazing Mr X (1948), Abraham Polonsky’s Force of Evil (1948), The Sound of Fury (1950), directed by Cy Endfield, Fred Zinnemann’s High Noon (1952), Charlie Chaplin’s A King in New York (1957), Hollywood on Trial (1976) by David Helpern, Martin Ritt’s The Front (1976) with Woody Allen, and 1996’s Red Hollywood , directed by Thom Andersen and Noël Burch. The 79th Locarno Film Festival runs Aug. 5-15. ‘The Front’ film still, courtesy of Park Circus/Sony Pictures Khoshbakht talked to THR about Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist , why it is “the timeliest” retrospective he has ever worked on, Hollywood’s role today, and the role of Charlie Chaplin and other stars in the showcase. Have you been working on this retrospective for Locarno for a long time, and how easy was the decision that the time was ripe for it? I had this project lined up for the future because it needed some proper research, but all of a sudden, I thought it was for now, because it’s about what’s happening right now. Even some of the terminology from back then is back in use. For instance, if you see press releases from the White House, there are some headlines with phrases that come right out of the McCarthy playbook, which is quite astonishing. They mention “the radical Left” and “radical propaganda,” among other things. But what is so interesting is that now both Left and Right, and the Center, have appropriated the terminology of that era to their own advantage. For instance, there was this Wall Street Journal headline saying basically: “McCarthyism is back – this time it’s woke.” So you can define McCarthyism as well, either as woke or anti-woke is McCarthyism. It’s just this confusion about the meaning of words and phrases that, back in the day, at least had some clear meaning – most of it completely wrong, but they were used in a very specific way. Curating retrospectives takes a lot of work and research. Can you share some insight into how long you researched this topic and these films? I had seen almost all of the films, so I knew my films, and that’s the most important part. But this is one of those subjects that comes with hundreds of books, and new books are being published every year. So, you want to catch up with the literature. There is also some other really interesting stuff, such as the declassified FBI files. That makes it far more exciting to dive into this episode in the history of American cinema. ‘Force of Evil’ film still, courtesy of Park Circus/Paramount There are also the oral histories and books that the victims of the blacklist, especially The Hollywood Ten, wrote from the late ’70s onwards about their own experience. There are contradictions, there are paradoxes, I guess a bit of egocentrism, but when you put them together with the rest, it gives you a relatively accurate picture of how things unfolded from ’47 onwards. I love the title you guys picked for the retrospective, Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist . How long did you think about what to call this showcase? Many good titles have been used by writers of books. One of those titles I love very much is Tender Comrades [: A Backstory of the Hollywood Blacklist ]. I thought the title should make clear that this is about not one subject, but actually two subjects. One is red, and one is black. Red is a reference to the Hollywood Left, which was active before the blacklist was introduced in 1947, and then black is for the blacklist. This is a program that actually studies the journey of the Hollywood Left from the early ’40s until the late ’60s. When Locarno unveiled this latest retrospective, you said this is the most timely retrospective you have put together. This is your third one for the Locarno festival, but you have done so much other work. How is this one different? It is my most timely retrospective so far, and it is something very special. The fact that we are talking about this is also special, because, sadly, The Hollywood Reporter was one of the key players in the blacklist episode, playing the role of a cheerleader for the FBI and for the [House of Representatives’ investigative committee known as the] House Un-American Activities Committee. ‘Native Son’ film still, courtesy of Kino Lorber If you asked me, if you put a gun to my head, why the blacklist happened, and I had to give you only one reason, I would tell you that it happened because of the union wars, because writers were successful in establishing the Screen Writers Guild, which Hollywood disliked very much, and which The Hollywood Reporter disliked. They didn’t want the writers to be powerful. The Hollywood Reporter didn’t miss any chance to attack the writers who were involved in the foundation of the Screen Writers Guild to the extent that in its reviews, when listing the cast and crew, it refused to list the name of the writer of the film, if it was someone like Dalton Trumbo. Some of these writers were making big money for Hollywood, like Trumbo, for instance, who was very well paid, and Ring Lardner Jr. In an attack directed at Lester Cole, they even published a front-page editorial by the editor of The Hollywood Reporter . And in that editorial, they mentioned his Communist Party membership number, which was secret information that even Cole didn’t have, because you didn’t really need that number. But the FBI had some spies in the Communist Party, and they had stolen that information, and that information was used. But it was not just The Hollywood Reporter . You had Catholic groups and others also campaigning behind the scenes. You have mentioned Trumbo and others. Some of the other faces and names that audiences will come across in the retrospective include the likes of John Garfield, Dorothy Parker and Charlie Chaplin. Can you talk about some of the big names and what roles they played? We have three different groups. One group is non-Americans, such as [German playwright] Bertolt Brecht, who testified [before the House Un-American Activities Committee], and the day after, he left the country for good. Otherwise, it would have been the Hollywood Eleven instead of The Hollywood Ten. But they couldn’t do much with him anyway because Brecht was not American, so the best they could have done was to deport him. But he was clever and said to hell with you, I’m going to go back home. Ehsan Khoshbakht, courtesy of Margherita Caprilli Courtesy of Margherita Caprilli Chaplin falls into that same category, because Chaplin was also not an American citizen. He was a British citizen. But the case with Chaplin is so unbelievably complex. Chaplin, even before the Communist Party of America started to gain more membership, was the subject of FBI surveillance. There are extensive records of him, and we are going to publish some of them in the book. They followed every movement of this man, because they were so afraid of him, in a sense, because he was perhaps the most popular and the most recognizable human figure on Earth. And he was very progressive. America was neutral at the beginning of the war, and the America First groups wanted to stay out of the war, but Chaplin, being British, was actively campaigning for the war. And then when America entered the war, Chaplin was campaigning for the Soviet allies, because that’s what President Roosevelt asked people to do to promote goodwill, because the U.S. needed the Soviets, and without them, they wouldn’t be able to win this war. And he was, you know, logistically, technically, absolutely right. So, so you have this group of non-Americans, and Chaplin is the most extreme case. The obsession with Chaplin, the anti-Semitic stories being circulated by the Hearst Media and the FBI about this man. Everything about him is so complex. Then you have a second group, which includes not the standard Hollywood people, but people who are also affected. This is the first time I’m showcasing the work of these people, too, such as [poet and writer] Dorothy Parker. She is not exactly a Hollywood person, but a celebrity, a writer, someone who stepped into Hollywood occasionally, but her world was mostly outside. I also have Richard Wright, the great African-American writer, in the program, and even Artie Shaw, the great jazz musician and bandleader. These are people who were affected by the blacklist. Artie Shaw, for example, went into self-imposed exile in Spain. David Halpern’s ‘Hollywood on Trial,’ courtesy of Corinth Films Courtesy of Corinth Films Finally, the third group has the very famous Hollywood people who were affected, the Hollywood Ten and beyond. It is much more than the Hollywood Ten in this program, because I think some of the people who were not part of the Hollywood Ten were actually far more interesting than some of its members. Film programs in the past refused to show works of people who named names, meaning people who eventually lost their integrity and became collaborators. But this program features works of such people as well because they were also believers. I think every program so far, perhaps unwittingly, has celebrated the idea of political martyrdom. I don’t believe in that, and I’m just interested in the Left, whether they stayed believers until the end or they just couldn’t take it anymore. One good example is Ben Maddow, one of the finest writers in Hollywood. After a while, he just couldn’t accept the fact that all these greatest scripts that he was writing were appearing on screen with the name of someone else. So he named names. I noticed that your retrospective is mixing genres and types of media, including not just films, but also old newsreels… Yes, I am trying to paint a more diverse but also broader and more accurate picture of the left and the blacklist in Hollywood. That’s why I decided to include many things, thanks to the UCLA Film & Television Archive, which is a partner in this. They have the best collection of material you can get on this subject. They have recently scanned original newsreels by Hearst Media, which was, in terms of media support of the witch hunt, at the forefront. Hearst Media produced many anti-communist newsreels and very harshly worded ones, in particular about the Hollywood Ten. I’m showing six of them. It’s very interesting because today, the word terrorist is used for anyone who is ideologically disliked and commits acts of violence. It should be easier to be able to say this person is a terrorist, and that person is “just” a criminal. And the term terrorist was used against communists in the ’40s, as we see in the news reels. It’s very interesting how these phrases sort of get recycled, and anyone opposing something you see as a person who poses a threat to your ideology. The word “terrorist” has been a standard term in American politics during the Trump administration. ‘The Hollywood Blacklist: The Survivors Tell Their Stories,’ courtesy of Cloud Studio SAS Your retrospective also mixes fiction and documentary features. What docs can audiences expect? There are going to be world premieres of two new documentaries. One is a documentary, driven by Eddie Muller, the writer and film noir expert. It is about Abraham Polonsky, who wrote some of the greatest films for blacklisted artists, but directed only one film, Force of Evil , before he was blacklisted. He couldn’t make another film until 20 years later, when he made Tell Them Willie Boy Is Here with Robert Redford. Eddie Muller believes he’s the greatest American writer. So there is this new feature documentary about him that has many great people, including directors and other Hollywood figures, talking about him. This film is called Dangerous Citizen : The Life and Times of Abraham Polonsky . The title comes from one of the declassified FBI files that said he was a very dangerous citizen. There’s also another documentary based on footage shot by a student during a party in Los Angeles in the early ’80s, where all the surviving members of the blacklist got together. This French woman, Marie- Dominique Montel, shot this footage and didn’t do anything with it until now, which is quite exciting. She’s been turning it into a documentary in color. So it will show us unseen footage of many of those Hollywood 10 people who were still alive then. The title is La Liste Noire d’Hollywood: Par ceux qui l’ont vécue , [or in English:] The Hollywood Blacklist: The Survivors Tell Their Stories . You mentioned the political situation and division in the U.S. of our day. How much political consciousness and activism do you see in current Hollywood? I have not seen every single film coming out of Hollywood, but some of the major titles that I have seen, for instance, Paul Thomas Anderson ‘s One Battle After Another , are open about it. I think he actually likes to study the period of the blacklist, because the film shows one of the many reincarnations of that culture of radical politics morphing into disillusionment and, in this case, political violence. ‘Dangerous Citizen: The Life and Times of Abraham Polonsky’ film still, courtesy of Black Pool Productions The Hollywood Left never transformed into something violent. And this is, I think, one of the great advantages that that movement had. If you compare films like Force of Evil , in which everybody and everything is corrupt from bottom to top, you will say, “Oh, Hollywood is very lame these days,” because nobody dares to paint a picture as bleak as some of these artists painted, especially in film noir and in crime thrillers. I think no period in Hollywood was as politically involved, within the confines of mass entertainment, as the ’30s and ’40s. However, you have far more political films made in Hollywood in the ’60s and ’70s. But the difference is that in the ’30s and ’40s, they were in the very heart of Hollywood, big titles that were making a case for change. in the ’60s and ’70s, when the definition of art house cinema became more prominent, it became something more niche, something for a specific group. Have you come across any particularly over-the-top, maybe even funny anecdotes in your research? In the FBI reports, they were also studying John Huston’s film The Treasure of the Sierra Madre, for which Huston won the best adapted screenplay and director Oscars, and his father, Walter Houston, won the best supporting actor Oscar. The FBI report says there’s one scene in the film in which Walter Houston [explains the value of gold using Marxist economic theory from Karl Marx’s Das Kapital, without directly mentioning it]. And they said you have to be very aware of these subversive messages. Don’t forget that these filmmakers came out of the Great Depression and saw people in kilometer-long queues for food, a cup of coffee, or a piece of bread. They saw abject poverty, broken families, suicide, and massive joblessness. And they were responding to that. That socialist attitude was in direct response to the way the capitalist economy failed in America, as well as elsewhere, in the early ’30s. You had a sort of activism not only in Hollywood but everywhere in that period when people were directly engaged with politics, joining the picket lines. Robert Rossen, the winner of the best film Oscar in 1949 for All the King’s Men , was on the frontline of any picket line during the strikes of the early ’40s. ‘None But the Lonely Heart’ film still, courtesy of Park Circus/Warner Bros. Did Hollywood studios have actual concerns with the creatives on the blacklist? Studios didn’t really believe that these writers were a threat. They gave in only when there was a huge amount of pressure from the outside. Their desire is to continue with these people because they are bringing money into the business and writing great scripts, for example, Trumbo and Lester Cole are very successful. They need them. They want them. So when the blacklist comes into effect, everything goes sort of underground. They continue writing, but under assumed names, and they keep winning Oscars. Trumbo is a great example of that. He won the Oscar twice after he got blacklisted [, namely for 1953’s Roman Holiday , initially credited to a front, and 1956’s The Brave One , credited to a pseudonym, Robert Rich], and one of those films is one with plenty of political messages. Do you maybe have an example of a film in the retrospective from creatives who named names, as you mentioned earlier? The most notorious of them is the 1954 film On the Waterfront . Three of the major talents involved in the making of that film are people who named names. There is Elia Kazan, the director who became a collaborator. There is Budd Schulberg, the screenwriter, who was a collaborator. And there is Lee J. Cobb, one of the actors in the film. This is a key film that, like many, used McCarthyism as the background for exploring fear, paranoia, and segregation in American society. The most famous example is High Noon , which is also in the program. Is there anything else you’d like to mention or highlight? We have a Western written by a woman, Karen DeWolf, in the retrospective. The film is called Silver Lode , which is similar to High Noon . It’s about a man who is about to get married, and then he’s accused of something, and he has to clear his name. He’s alone, and the whole town turns against him. These have all been seen until now as allegories of McCarthyism. But one of the reasons I’m doing these programs is that there are all these ideas. Now watch a film and see whether you see it as an allegory of McCarthyism or something else. It could be something else. The positive thing about the retrospective is that you have the chance to test certain ideas, to examine them again and see how accurate they are. THR

title: Sadie Sink’s Secret Role in ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Finally Revealed
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 30, 2026 10:00pm Sadie Sink and 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day.' Kevin Winter/Getty Images; Everett Collection Logo text [This story contains spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day .] Sadie Sink ‘s top-secret-ish role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day has finally been revealed. The reason I say “ish” is because despite Marvel and Sink remaining tight-lipped, fan rumors have been swirling about her casting since even before the first trailer that dropped in March included a two-second clip of a mystery person in a green jacket. This led fans to speculate that Sink was playing powerful mutant Jean Grey, as the character is known to have fiery red hair (much like Sink) and wear the color green, at least in some of her classic comic book appearances. Related Stories Movies Spider-Man: The Last Blockbuster Franchise Hollywood Hasn't Screwed Up Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Aims to Make Box Office History as It Targets High-Flying Opening Now that the Tom Holland -led film has hit theaters, I’m happy to congratulate those behind the rumors for being correct. Throughout the Brand New Day press tour leading up to the film’s release on July 31, the Stranger Things actress seemingly dodged all questions surrounding any specifics of her role. Earlier this month, during an interview with The Hollywood Reporter , director Destin Daniel Cretton shared that all the secrecy with Sink’s character has to do with the moviegoing experience. “Keeping what Sadie’s doing under wraps, you’ll honestly understand when you see the movie. The movie is a better movie if you don’t know certain things,” he said. “I wish people didn’t know anything when they go in to watch this movie, but we’re not doing it for any other reason but to protect the experience of the fans. And whoever goes on opening weekend, you are going to have a much cooler experience if you go in not knowing certain things.” Brand New Day has Holland back in the Spidey suit, with Zendaya and Jacob Batalon also reprising their roles as MJ and Ned, respectively. The fourth installment, coming off the box office success of 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home , sees Peter Parker living entirely alone as Spider-Man in a world that doesn’t remember him. That’s until mounting pressure of seeing his old friends move on without him triggers a dangerous change, while a powerful new villain emerges. Last year, while chatting with THR , Sink admitted she was looking forward to when she could finally talk about her Spider-Man role, as “There’s so much I want to share.” “Spider-Man has always been my favorite,” she said at the time. “I love Spider-Man. I love Tom’s Spider-Man, especially. To be a fan of something and then join it is a familiar feeling for me, because I was a fan of Stranger Things before I joined the show, but I was super excited about what they had planned. I also worked with the director, Destin Daniel Cretton, in one of the first movies I ever did when I was 14, so it’s kind of a full-circle moment. I had an amazing time working on that film.” Spider-Man: Brand New Day is currently playing in theaters. THR

title: ‘Pachinko’ Star Kim Minha to Host Busan Film Festival’s Opening Ceremony
full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 30, 2026 9:34pm Kim Minha Myunggu Han/Getty Images for Apple TV+ Pachinko star Kim Minha will host the gala opening ceremony of this year’s Busan International Film Festival . Asia ‘s leading cinema event customarily features two Korean stars at its kick-off event, but organizers revealed Friday that Kim will hold down the duties solo when BIFF raises its curtain on Oct. 6. Busan launched its first-ever main competition section last year for its landmark 30th edition. This year’s event will continue to try to build momentum for the section, establishing the Busan Awards Grand Prize as Asia’s premier cinema honor. Related Stories Business Europe to Boycott World Cup in FIFA Protest Movies Andy Garcia's Starry L.A. Noir 'Diamond' Lands at Sony Pictures Classics Kim is best known worldwide as young Sunja in Pachinko , Apple TV’s sweeping adaptation of Min Jin Lee’s bestselling novel, in which she shared the saga’s central role across timelines with Oscar winner Youn Yuh-jung. The part, spanning the series’ two seasons in 2022 and 2024, turned the actress — who debuted in 2016 — into one of the most closely watched young talents in Korean film and television. She has stayed busy since, with credits including the Dinsney+ series Light Shop , TVING’s Way Back Love and Typhoon Family on Netflix, along with this year’s film Hana Korea . She won best actress in the international competition at the 2025 Seoul International Drama Awards and best new actress at the 2025 Blue Dragon Series Awards. In announcing the appointment, BIFF credited the “depth and emotional precision she brings to every role” and her growing stature as a star of Korea’s new generation. “Known for her poised yet spirited presence, she is expected to bring warmth and confidence to the opening ceremony and set the tone for this year’s festival,” organizers said in a statement. BIFF’s 31st edition runs Oct. 6-15 at the Busan Cinema Center and other venues across the South Korean port city. THR

title: Ariana Grande’s ‘Petal’ Introduces an Angry and Angular Ari: Album Review
full_text: Jul 30, 2026 9:15pm PT Ariana Grande’s ‘Petal’ Introduces an Angry and Angular Ari: Album Review By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Music Industry Moves: Influence Media Partners to Acquire Anthem Entertainment’s Publishing and Film & TV Assets in $600 Million Deal 14 hours ago Ryan Bingham Signs With WME (EXCLUSIVE) 22 hours ago Grammy Chief ‘Saddened to Hear’ That BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Awards 1 day ago See All On the surface, Ariana Grande ’s “Petal” is a sister album to its predecessor, 2024’s “Eternal Sunshine” — it was made with the same two collaborators, Ilya Salmanzadeh and Max Martin, and it also was entirely written, performed and produced by the three of them. Usually, that formula means a chapter two: more of the same but different. Not this time. This sister is darker, moodier and a lot more blunt than “Sunshine,” and her emotions are more volatile, less heartbroken, and much less internalized. It’s a different Ariana, musically and especially lyrically. Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement Grande braced her fans for a change in a widely circulated interview earlier this week. “I think [fans] will feel familiarity and comfort in it,” she said of the album. “Yet at the same time it’s very experimental and different for me, and also I wrote from a place that I don’t usually, which is unfiltered rage,” she laughed. “I usually am too shy to tap into that, and I think this time I didn’t filter as much as I usually do.” Popular on Variety “This is rage?,” some may think at first listen, because it’s still a pop album, even though it moves into weirder territory musically than she has in the past. And let’s be real: With her pretty, pristine soprano, it’s hard to imagine what an Angry Ari (“AngRI”?) would sound like. But lurking below the shiny surface of many of the songs are lyrics like: “Just know that I will find my way from you like flowers from a tomb”; “All of my favorite stories end in some kind of catastrophe”; “I’m not a victim, bitch, I’m practically drowning in my blessings”; “Good luck on your way to hell.” Likewise, the NSFW lyrics of her recent albums moves into a whole new realm: “Pussy so sweet a tear fell from his eye”; “This sex is bout to make a grown man cry”; “The grass is way greener since I been beneath ya”; and if those were too subtle, “No one fucks you like I do.” And for good measure, there’s a mission statement: “Keep my heels tall, my ego small, but I’m still Grande.” The heartbroken but resilient Grande from the last album is nowhere in sight — with one exception, these songs are about vengeance or sex, and about whom is bound to be the subject of endless online chatter. The album’s lead single, “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” is a solid introduction to the sound of the album’s more experimental tracks: It’s beautiful but odd, with a crinkling synthesizer hook over a spare beat, creating an haunting setting for her lush, multitracked vocals; her growth as a melodicist is on full display in the mellifluous, multisyllabic middle section. As she promised, there are familiar-sounding songs and moments (“Kiss Me,” “Freak”), but there’s also music that would be more expected from FKA Twigs or even the Weeknd — Ilya executive-produced the album with Grande (Martin contributes to just three songs), so his more-adventurous inclinations have come to the fore. “Like I Do,” probably the album’s darkest song musically, is based around the lovely eight-note wordless figure she sings at the beginning, but soon gives way to an ominous, hulking rhythm musical track; several songs are built around Ilya’s trademark malfunctioning-computer synth lines. The hard-hitting title track pairs a busy, complex melody with a thudding Portishead rhythm; it’s like two different songs playing in synch. But even relatively straightforward songs don’t sound like anything she’s done before. “Never Get Over Me” has an icy funk groove with a silky soulful vocal — and, far off in the distance, that psycho siren-like sound from “Kill Bill” (thematic link!) whenever Beatrix Kiddo is about to act out her unfiltered rage. “Bad Thing (Bunny Hop)” is a fast, new wave-esque track with a flash of “Blinding Lights”; “Big Feelings” has a sultriness that we have rarely heard from her in the past. The one exception is the closing track and prettiest song, the ballad “Nowhere, Nobody,” driven by a heavily echoed guitar and a percolating rhythm track, a showcase for Grande’s lush, layered vocals, which bring back the wistfulness of “Eternal Sunshine.” It, and the album, end on an English-teacher-enraging note by quite deliberately finishing with a preposition: “There’s nowhere else and there is nobody else/ that I’d rather be … with.” “Petal” is not an easy or obvious career move — it’s probably the biggest musical departure of her career, but it’s also her most musically and lyrically accomplished album. She continues to grow as a virtuoso singer and vocal arranger, soaring to the top of her range with ease, but also showing nuance in her emotion as well as the kind of innovation she showed on the elaborate singing-along-with-herself loops featured on the “Sunshine” tour. Eight albums into her discography, Ariana Grande continues to surprise. title: Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21%
full_text: Jul 30, 2026 8:58pm PT Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% Company raises guidance for FY 2026 operating income by 8%, citing higher expected profitability in PlayStation games segment By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% 7 hours ago Disney Expected to Sell 50% Stake in A+E to Hearst for More Than $1 Billion 13 hours ago Apple Sales Rise 16% to Record $109 Billion for June Quarter, Services Revenue Falls Short of Forecasts 14 hours ago See All Kristoffer Tripplaar/ Sipa USA Sony Pictures Entertainment posted a sales decline for the June 2026 quarter, offset by growth at Crunchyroll, while Sony’s music segment saw revenue increase 21%. The PlayStation games unit had flat sales for the period and a 37% increase in operating income driven by U.S. tariff refunds. Revenue for Sony Pictures for the quarter ended June 30 was $1.978 billion, down 13% year over, while operating income rose 21% to $156 million. The company said the sales decline was due to a decrease in series deliveries in television productions — revenue was down 32%, to $571 million. SPE also had lower revenue from theatrical releases: $30 million in the most recent quarter from its sole release in the period (TriStar’s comedy “The Breadwinner”) vs. $132 million from four releases in the year-earlier period. Total revenue in the Motion Pictures group was $645 million for the June quarter (-13%). Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement The higher revenue from anime streaming service Crunchyroll was mainly due to paid subscriber growth. As of the end of March, the service had more than 21 million paid subscribers, and Sony said it continued to gain subs in the June quarter. Popular on Variety Overall for the quarter, Sony’s Q1 of fiscal year 2026, the company posted revenue of 2.837 trillion yen ($17.8 billion), up 8%, and net income of 342.2 billion yen ($2.15 billion), up 32%. For full-year fiscal 2026, Sony upped its consolidated operating income forecast by 8%, to 1.72 trillion yen ($10.8 billion), citing ​an expected increase in profitability in the PlayStation business. A major gaming title release coming this November is Take-Two Interactive’s “Grand Theft Auto VI,” which should provide a lift to the PlayStation division. Sony raised guidance for FY26 total revenue by 2%, to 12.5 trillion yen ($78.5 billion) compared with 12.48 trillion yen in FY25. In the PlayStation division, sales for the June quarter were flat at 937.1 billion yen ($5.88 billion) and operating income rose 37%, to 202.0 billion yen ($1.27 billion), lifted by the impact of U.S. tariff refunds after the Supreme Court invalidated President Trump’s global tariffs in February 2026. Total PlayStation monthly active users reached 125 million accounts in June, up 2% year over year. Total playtime during the quarter decreased 4% from the year-prior period, but Sony said “user engagement continued to be solid” and noting a tough comparison with Q1 of FY25, which “benefited from season updates to major titles and new hit titles.” It sold 1.5 million PS5 units in the June quarter compared with 2.5 million in the year-earlier period. Sony’s music segment pulled in revenue of 562.0 billion yen ($3.53 billion), an increase of 21%. That was led by the impact of foreign exchange rates; higher revenue from live events and merchandising in recorded music; and a bump in streaming revenue. For the June quarter, streaming revenue growth rates on a U.S. dollar basis were up 10% year-on-year for recorded music and up 8% for music publishing. Operating income for the music segment rose 14% to 105.9 billion yen ($665 million). The average exchange rate used for Sony’s June quarter figures was 159.3 yen to $1 U.S. dollar. Regarding the recent Kumamoto earthquake, Sony said it has several semiconductor facilities located in Kumamoto prefecture and neighboring prefectures. “While all these facilities were affected by the earthquake, there were no major casualties,” the company said. Sony’s production sites in Nagasaki, Oita and Kagoshima had no significant damage to buildings or equipment and production has resumed. title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Credits Scene Explained: Will Tom Holland Return in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ or ‘Secret Wars’?
full_text: Jul 30, 2026 8:00pm PT ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Credits Scene Explained: Will Tom Holland Return in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ or ‘Secret Wars’? By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Credits Scene Explained: Will Tom Holland Return in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ or ‘Secret Wars’? 8 hours ago ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: Sadie Sink Is [SPOILER]. How Her Role Sets Up Marvel’s Next Reboot 11 hours ago ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’s’ Breakout, Ryan Reynolds’ Jeanpool Stunt and More Comic-Con Highlights 3 days ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ,” now playing in theaters. Where in the world is Spider-Man going next? After saving New York City in “Brand New Day,” Tom Holland ‘s friendly neighborhood Spider-Man looks like he’s heading off-world once again. The post-credits scene in the latest Sony and Marvel movie revealed that the hero will return to the MCU and seems to be leaving Earth in his next appearance. Related Stories Byron Allen Donates $100,000 to Nolan Wells Family's GoFundMe as Tyler Perry Covers Funeral Costs Tyler Perry's 'Beauty in Black' Gets Surprise Season 4 Renewal After Final Season Announcement First, like many fans have theorized for months, Sadie Sink is playing X-Men member Jean Grey in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” She’s the primary antagonist in the movie, though it’s later revealed that the Department of Damage Control kidnapped and killed her older sister Sara. Once he realizes the cause of Jean’s Damage Control crusade, Spider-Man convinces her to release the psychic bubble she creates that freezes nearly every New Yorker at the end of the movie. He also saves her from getting shot by Jon Bernthal’s Punisher and gets hit by the sniper rifle bullet himself. At the end of the movie, Spidey recuperates, and Jean heads out of town (and possibly to Xavier’s School for Gifted Youngsters upstate). Popular on Variety In the final moments of the movie, Holland’s Peter Parker runs into his former best friend Ned (Jacob Batalon) at a cafe. Due to Doctor Strange’s spell at the end of “No Way Home,” the world has forgotten who Peter is, so Ned only recognizes the stranger after he crashed his house party earlier in the movie. With nothing to lose, Peter reintroduces himself to Ned and they perform their secret handshake without missing a beat. All of a sudden, Ned seems to regain his memories of Peter just as the film ends. Does that mean Zendaya’s MJ could also remember Peter? Could true love’s kiss actually reawaken her love for him? Earlier in the movie, it’s also revealed that Ned has created a Spidey-tracking app that he uses to follow the hero’s location. During the post-credits scene, the app reappears as it attempts to pinpoint where the wall-crawler is. However, the Spidey Tracker starts to zoom out so far that it’s clear Spider-Man isn’t in New York City or even on Earth. The app locates the hero out in space, and then the movie announces that “Spider-Man will return” — but it’s unclear when or how. Currently, Holland isn’t on the call sheet for the sprawling cast of “ Avengers: Doomsday .” The team-up film brings together many of the A-listers on the Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men and Thunderbolts teams, but no Holland. However, that doesn’t count out a surprise appearance or cameo from the web-slinger, especially considering the entire MCU is coming together to battle Robert Downey Jr.’s evil mastermind Doctor Doom. If Holland doesn’t reappear in “Doomsday,” then the post-credits scene could point to a role in “Avengers: Secret Wars,” the follow-up scheduled for next year. If the movie follows the comic run of the same name, it could bring together every hero from across the MCU multiverse into one dimension called Battleworld. In the comics, Battleworld stitched together all the different worlds and plopped every hero and their variant into one new universe. If the MCU followed suit, that could be the reason the Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men are eventually able to share one universe. Could that also bring together past Spider-Man stars Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield, who crossed over into “No Way Home”? Fans will have to wait and see in “Secret Wars,” but that could be how Holland lands his next MCU appearance. LISTEN: Credit Risks: Top S&P Global Analyst Breaks Down the Paramount-Warner Bros. title: The Affordability Squeeze Has Come for Brandy Melville’s TikTok Star Staffer
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kevin Dolak Plus Icon Kevin Dolak View All July 30, 2026 6:35pm Brandy Melville store on July 7, 2024. Photo by Cristina Arias/Cover/Getty Images The creator economy met the affordability squeeze this week in New York when TikTok darling and Brandy Melville SoHo staffer Allegra Pinkowitz was unceremoniously fired from her position with the controversial fast-fashion retailer after nearly two and a half years. While one may not think the part-time retail gig of a high school junior is notable news, Pinkowitz is also an up-and-coming TikToker with a following of 162K-plus. Last year, she was the subject of a New York magazine article titled “The Most Popular Girl in SoHo is a Brandy Melville Employee,” about the flocks of girls who have been showing up to watch her fold clothes during weekend shifts or after school. Related Stories Lifestyle Disney and Old Navy Team Up for New Haunted Halloween Line of Cozy Flannels, PJs and Totes Music Boy George Drops Out of London 'Jesus Christ Superstar' Production After Stirring Controversy With AI-Generated Pro-Israel Song When Pinkowitz received the news from a male manager by phone on Thursday, she was on TikTok faster than you can say vibecession. After an announcement clip set to rapper ASN JAYBOOG’s “Stanley Earl,” she was back hours later to dish on how it all went down. “This was so unexpected. You guys don’t understand — I’ve been working there for almost two and a half years,” she explains in the clip as she applies makeup; she told her fans she was about to get in the shower when a text arrived. @allegrasgrwm my @Katie Fang moment #nyc ♬ original sound – allegra “It’s basically like, ‘Can you just give me a call whenever you have a minute?’ … He’s basically like, ‘We didn’t make as much money as we were hoping to this summer, so we’re laying off a bunch of people,'” she explained in a series of video cuts of her doing her beauty ritual. “It was just basically, ‘But I’ll hold on to your contact, and if anything comes up in the fall, maybe you can come back.’ This was extremely unexpected.” Pinkowitz, whose TikTok fame drew crowds of upward of 20 fans at a time to Brandy Melville’s flagship lower Broadway store, was told that her firing had nothing to do with her work ethic. She added that the layoff “stings more because I’ve always talked really positively about this brand online,” and reassured her followers that she wasn’t there to hate on the brand. “I’m so sad. I expected a little bit more loyalty, but now I’m in the market for a new job,” the teenager said, holding back tears at moments throughout the clip. A first firing is always tough, but for Brandy Melville’s fanbase, the job loss means a central figure of the SoHo scene is gone. Criticized after switching to a more California-centric style for its one-size-fits-all apparel (it’s a small) and for reportedly favoring conventionally attractive, mostly blonde staff, the Italy-founded and now U.S.-based brand known for bleached wood, muted tones and T-shirts reading “NANTUCKET” saw further backlash after an investigative Business Insider story was published and later adapted into a 2024 documentary for HBO Max, called Brandy Hellville & the Cult of Fast Fashion . The film, in which Pinkowitz appears, features staffers discussing the body dysmorphia they developed while working for Brandy Melville and trying to fit into its image and its small clothing — sizing that was eventually changed to a tone-deaf “one-size-fits-most.” Pinkowitz’s recounting of the call — in which the manager cited lagging sales as the reason for layoffs — is hard to square with the many accounts of a mobbed SoHo location with lines out the door. It’s difficult to imagine all those tweens stopping in to catch a glimpse of Pinkowitz without buying anything. In 2025, Brandy Melville’s annual sales reached $283 million, with steady 10 to 15 percent year-over-year growth. Retail analysts say the brand’s business model yields unusually high profit margins, thanks largely to its one-size-fits-most approach and its social-media-driven marketing strategy. THR

News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath As Stuart Fails To Save the Universe revealed in the Episode 2 opening credits spoiler (You can read all about the show’s unique, ever-changing main title sequence here ), “Zack is in this one.” Zack, a recurring character on The Big Bang Theory played by Brian Thomas Smith, was Penny’s ( Kaley Cuoco ) dim-witted but kind-hearted on- and off- boyfriend while she and Leonard (Johnny Galecki) were broken up. Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , from The Big Bang Theory creators Chuck Lorre & Bill Prady and Zak Penn , has established a pattern with the first two episodes, each featuring a surprise return of a Big Bang Theory original cast member. Following Kunal Nayyar’s appearance as Raj in Episode 1 where he is shockingly killed by Kripke (John Ross Bowie), Cuoco showed up in the second episode alongside Zack (Smith). In it, Penny is a leader of the resistance against an AI-imposed mind control in an alternate universe where everyone is forced to be perpetually nice and happy by shock-inducing buttons on their necks. Zack is her second in command. (L-R): Brian Posehn, Brian Thomas Smith, Kevin Sussman , Kaley Cuoco and John Ross Bowie in Episode 2 of ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ Multiverse and all, why did the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators opt to have Penny be with Zack as if her relationship with Leonard — one of the hallmarks of The Big Bang Theory from the pilot — never happened? “Because that’s what happened in that universe, we don’t know what Leonard is doing in that universe,” Prady said. “Every universe gives every character a completely different history. There’s no continuity because they lived a different life, they lived in a different world. That Penny lives in a world where an evil AI controls people through shock collars, and so she had a completely different experience.” Added Lorre, “There was no Cheesecake Factory in her life,” a reference to Penny’s place of work for most of Big Bang ‘s run. Stuart Fails To Save the Universe presents a very different version of Penny who is pretty ruthless, violently slapping Stuart (Kevin Sussman), Bert (Brian Posehn) and Kripke (John Ross Bowie) to “deprogram” them and ordering them killed with no hesitation once she realizes that they don’t know how to defeat the AI overlord. The trio are ultimately saved by a drone attack launched by the AI, with Penny, Zack and the rest getting incapacitated while Stuart, Bert, Kripke, along with Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), use Leonard and Sheldon’s machine to transport themselves to another universe. With Raj teetering on the edge of madness in Season 1, are Big Bang OGs relishing going dark in the spinoff? “Beyond,” Prady said. Added Lorre, “Beyond. It was fun to do something different, that was part of the promise, come and play with us, and we’ll make sure that you’re playing a version of your character you never got to play before, an entirely different approach to the character, and that was fun for the actors.” Said Penn, “And everyone wants to play the bad guy, that’s always the most fun role.” Episode 2 also includes appearances from The Big Bang Theory ‘s Christine Baranski and Riki Lindhome. Baranski, who played Leonard’s mom Beverly on the mothership series, is the host of the 30-month re-education program Stuart, Bert are Kripke are forced to attend as a version of herself. Related Stories News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’: Here Is Why Episodes Of ‘Big Bang Theory’ Spinoff Are So Short After Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ) got separated from Stuart ( Kevin Sussman ), Bert ( Brian Posehn ) and Kripke ( John Ross Bowie ) at the end of the first episode of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe as the guys were transported from the post-apocalyptic CalTech lab to an alternate universe, Stuart made it his mission to find Denise — or that alternate reality’s version of her. He tracked her down to find her “happily” married to Gary (Tommy Walker), the same guy who was Denise’s boyfriend in post-apocalyptic Pasadena in the premiere where he was senselessly killed by CalTech guards. Happily is in quotes because in that universe, society is ruled by an evil AI through a buzzer on everyone’s neck which sends electric shocks through their body if they express any negative emotion. “Denise, you and I are destined to be together, and I have come from a parallel universe to claim you,” Stuart said while sitting in Denise and Gary’s living room. Deadline asked Sussman about Stuart’s gutsy move. ”That’s interesting that you bring that up because that’s pretty un-Stuart like,” he said. “So I guess if there is some growth for Stuart, it’s that his love for her pushes him into a kind of assertiveness that he never would have had on the original show.” Lupkus spoke about Denise’s unhappy marriage, which had driven her to drinking, and Stuart’s arrival. “In that universe, we have buzzers on our necks that stop us from ever being rude or saying what like anything that’s not totally happy, so she’s conditioned at that point to just act like everything’s fine, and to have someone coming into her apartment saying like, you don’t have to live like this like, I’m gonna get you out of here, she can’t even react because she knows that she’ll just be writhing on the floor,” Lapkus said. “So I think, as we see later, she gets swept up in it with him, but then her real feelings for him start to return, and she can feel again.” Added Sussman, ” Yeah, and it actually is a good metaphor for anybody who’s ever felt stuck in a relationship.” What about Gary? Once again, he was left behind as by the end of the episode, Denise had joined Stuart, Bert and Kripke, and she and Stuart were seen holding hands while leaping into the next universe together. “I think Denise has some sort of love for Gary, even if he’s the wrong guy for her, because she’s excited to see him every time she sees him, and she’s back with him over and over again,” Lapkus said. “There are those people in your life where you’re like, you got to break up with that guy, but she kind of likes him for some weird reason, and then she cares for him, so when he’s killed over and over, that’s also pretty upsetting.” Added Sussman, “It’s bad enough when your loved one is murdered once.” Unveils First Results Since Sky Deal; Studios Biz Bullish Despite U.S. Declines Fremantle Hires ‘Narcos’ Exec As Global Scripted Chief Disney Selling A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst In Billion-Dollar Deal ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s $309M Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe July 30, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple July 23, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators & Stars On Premiere’s Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Panel Teases DC Episode, OG Returns As ‘Big Bang Theory…
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary? Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board View All July 23, 2026 5:33pm Story Arc (L-R) Kevin Sussman, Lauren Lapkus and John Ross Bowie speak at HBO Max's "Stuart Fails To Save The Universe" Hall H panel during 2026 Comic-Con International: San Diego at San Diego Convention Center on July 23, 2026 in San Diego, California. Amy Sussman/Getty Images Eight years after the cast of The Big Bang Theory made their last Comic-Con appearance ahead of the hit CBS sitcom’s 12th and final season, four Big Bang actors were back at the comic book convention with spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . The single-camera offshoot’s leads, Kevin Sussman (Stuart), Lauren Lapkus (Denise), John Ross Bowie (Kripke) and Brian Posehn (Bert) were joined on the Hall H stage by series creators Chuck Lorre and Bill Prady, who also co-created Big Bang , and Zak Penn. During a panel after a screening of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ‘s premiere episode, Prady promised more appearances by Big Bang alums. Related Stories Books Co-Founders Of Magic Hour Entertainment And Rebelle Media Plus Author Duo Christina Lauren Advise Studios & Streamers To Devote Resources To "Elevated" And "Prestige" Romance Through Casting, Chemistry & More News Ryan Reynolds Thanks 'Deadpool' Fans For "Unapologetic Devotion" After Undercover Comic-Con Appearance - Watch Video “Well, you saw one wonderful member of the the Big Bang Theory family in that first episode,” he said. “There are more, and there are also some performers who are some wonderful minor characters that are coming back.” Watch on Deadline A number of them are in the show’s official trailer , released last month. Making a “drive-by” appearance at the panel was DC Comics’ Publisher and Chief Creative Officer Jim Lee who teased a DC-focused episode of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe. “They requested some DC characters to be involved in an episode,” he said. We saw a glimpse of that in the trailer, which features Mr. Freeze. “It was just amazing that they were trying to do something that was true to our characters, but at the same time find comedy in it,” Lee continued. “What was funny is we had scheduled the set visit to come to the set, and I just see the dialogue, the script. And when I came to the set, I was just blown away. It was completely not what I was expecting, I was expecting a multi-cam setup where they were sitting around, and then they start showing the visual effects that they were going to do, and all the bespoke elements they added to [Stuart’s comic book] store.” Added Lee, “Then Bill start talking about the overall arc of the 10 episodes, and I thought this is super ambitious, this is completely not what I expected. It’s like nerds going through Gulliver’s Travels , and I was sold. I was like, this is awesome, this is fantastic.” Lee closed out with praise for how the show handles the DC IP. “Some of the DC characters they have in it, I think are some of the best versions I’ve seen of those characters, and so I’m super excited for you guys,” he said. Inspired by the set visit, Lee created the cover for an exclusive Stuart Failed to Save the Universe comic book, which is also featured on the show. DC’s Jim Lee made a surprise appearance in Hall H at #SDCC to tease some DC comic book characters who audiences will see in ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe,’ which he says are “some of the best” versions of these characters he’s seen. pic.twitter.com/2EOpismjHi — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 23, 2026 Elsewhere on the panel, Lorre said that the goal with Stuart Fails To Save the Universe was to “try to make a science-fiction comedy that the characters of The Big Bang Theory would watch and argue about.” Questioning reality after his experience on the show, star Sussman spoke about being summoned by Lorre in 2022 for a meeting where the comedy uber producer pitched him the idea for Stuart Fails To Save the Universe. “That was nice of him to make it seem like I might say no,” Sussman quipped. ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ star Kevin Sussman jokes that the many iterations of the Comic Center of Pasadena are starting to make him question reality. “Are you real?” he asks Hall H at #SDCC before reminiscing on the early days of the spinoff’s conception. pic.twitter.com/18vCKXUoNx — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 23, 2026 In Stuart Fails To Save the Universe, which premieres July 23 on HBO Max, comic bookstore owner Stuart Bloom (Sussman) is tasked with restoring reality after he breaks a device built by Sheldon and Leonard, accidentally bringing about a multiverse Armageddon. Stuart is aided in this quest by his girlfriend Denise (Lapkus), geologist friend Bert (Posehn), and quantum physicist/all-around pain in the ass Barry Kripke (Bowie). Along the way, they meet alternate-universe versions of characters we’ve come to know and love from The Big Bang Theory. As the title implies, things don’t go well. Katie Campione contributed to this report. title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ EPs & Composer On Show’s Ever-Changing Title Sequence You…
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' $50M+ U.S. Previews Amazing, Ahead of 'No Way Home' Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board Disney Selling A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst In Billion-Dollar Deal View All July 23, 2026 6:30pm Story Arc 'Stuart Fails to Save The Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes a detail about the premiere episode of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Each episode of The Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe tells a story of its four protagonists, Stuart ( Kevin Sussman ), Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), Bert ( Brian Posehn ) and Kripke ( John Ross Bowie ), traveling to another alternate reality as they try to fix the device built by Sheldon and Leonard and the multiverse Armageddon it created. Each episode’s opening credits also tell their own story via a series of fourth wall-busting amusing messages to the viewer embedded into the animated title sequence set to a differently arranged theme song by Danny Elfman. The series of notes are capped by a spoiler, which in the Episode 1 credits reads “Barry Dies.” Related Stories Casting 'The Earliest Show': Chris Pratt, Lamorne Morris & Sarah Silverman Among 14 Guest Stars News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Creators & Stars On Premiere's Shocking OG Death & Its Aftermath Who is Barry? He turned out to be Denise’s boyfriend in post-apocalyptic Pasadena who dies pretty meaninglessly when he says “Follow me!” and charges first into the heavily guarded CalTech, leading Stuart and Bert, joined by Denise, in their mission to break in and take Sheldon and Leonard’s machine. While the title sequence spoiled one death, the series’ premiere featured a bigger, more shocking killing of an original Big Bang character, Raj (Kunal Nayyar), who had been imprisoned at CalTech by Barry Kripke (Bowie). You can read all about it here . Deadline asked Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators Chuck Lorre, Bill Prady and Zak Penn about the clever, custom title sequences. DEADLINE: Was this about one of you being really unhappy with the streaming culture of people skipping opening credits? LORRE : Me. PRADY : Chuck said people make these brilliant opening credit sequences that people watch one time. LORRE : And then you can click on the button that says ‘Skip Titles’, and I went, “Well, it’s a terrible waste of time and money and creativity. What if we made a title sequence that you could skip but you shouldn’t? And that would mean every title sequence have to be different and worth watching. And then we got a gift from the gods when Danny Elfman said yes, I’ll write a theme and produce a theme song, and he rearranged it and and remixed it and did variations on it throughout the 10 episodes as well, so the end result was a title sequence that hopefully is surprising and fun to watch. DEADLINE: And the spoiler part, where did it come from? Chuck, was it you again? Because some of them are really spoilers; ‘Barry Dies’ is a real spoiler. PENN : Yeah, that was I think something we all liked the idea of right off the bat is, why not? Who cares? We were like, let’s try it. Let’s just see what happens if we put a spoiler in the title, and we were just trying to keep ourselves entertained and do things that were different. PRADY : I mean, not much more than it made us laugh, the notion that, especially in the online television watching culture, there’s all of this stuff about spoilers, people hunting for spoilers, people trying to avoid spoilers. What if there’s a spoiler and it’s just sort of kind of meaningless? PENN : Also, I always felt like if we say “Spoiler: Gary Dies,” a lot of people are going to think, well, It’s not going to be that simple. So it would still be shocking when he actually does die. I’m counting on people being cynical about it. LORRE : I’m counting on people laughing. PRADY : The answer to a lot of questions is because it made us laugh, and we hope it makes other people laugh. DEADLINE: Some of the spoilers are really mild, but this one was like, first: who’s Gary?, and then it was that simple, he just died. PRADY : He died, didn’t he? And he really just died. PENN : Yeah, it’s just totally pointless. LORRE : “Follow me.” PRADY: “Follow me.” Oh. Musical Variations The Simpsons theme composer Elfman recalled “the crazy thing” that happened after he was asked to write main title music for Stuart Fails To Save the Universe and, as a Big Bang fan, agreed to do it. “I wrote it, Chuck loved it, and he said, ‘So here’s the thing. I need you to do 10 variations on it,'” Elfman said. “I thought about it for two seconds. No one’d ever asked me to do that before but I just said, ‘You got it.'” And he did it, drawing inspiration from the particular episode for its unique theme music. “It wasn’t even difficult,” he said. “Each episode, just mix it up and try things. It was really just fun.” Danny Elfman recalls how Chuck Lorre requested 10 different variations of the 'Stuart Fails to Save the Universe' theme: "No one's ever asked me to do that before" pic.twitter.com/MmlmZScV7o — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 22, 2026 Unveils First Results Since Sky Deal; Studios Biz Bullish Despite U.S. Declines Fremantle Hires ‘Narcos’ Exec As Global Scripted Chief Disney Selling A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst In Billion-Dollar Deal ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s $309M Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe July 30, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple July 30, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary? While the title sequence spoiled one death, the series’ premiere featured a bigger, more shocking killing of an original Big Bang character, Raj (Kunal Nayyar), who had been imprisoned at CalTech by Barry Kripke (Bowie). You can read all about it here . Deadline asked Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators Chuck Lorre, Bill Prady and Zak Penn about the clever, custom title sequences. DEADLINE: Was this about one of you being really unhappy with the streaming culture of people skipping opening credits? LORRE : Me. PRADY : Chuck said people make these brilliant opening credit sequences that people watch one time. LORRE : And then you can click on the button that says ‘Skip Titles’, and I went, “Well, it’s a terrible waste of time and money and creativity. What if we made a title sequence that you could skip but you shouldn’t? And that would mean every title sequence have to be different and worth watching. And then we got a gift from the gods when Danny Elfman said yes, I’ll write a theme and produce a theme song, and he rearranged it and and remixed it and did variations on it throughout the 10 episodes as well, so the end result was a title sequence that hopefully is surprising and fun to watch. DEADLINE: And the spoiler part, where did it come from? Chuck, was it you again? Because some of them are really spoilers; ‘Barry Dies’ is a real spoiler. PENN : Yeah, that was I think something we all liked the idea of right off the bat is, why not? Who cares? We were like, let’s try it. Let’s just see what happens if we put a spoiler in the title, and we were just trying to keep ourselves entertained and do things that were different. PRADY : I mean, not much more than it made us laugh, the notion that, especially in the online television watching culture, there’s all of this stuff about spoilers, people hunting for spoilers, people trying to avoid spoilers. What if there’s a spoiler and it’s just sort of kind of meaningless? PENN : Also, I always felt like if we say “Spoiler: Gary Dies,” a lot of people are going to think, well, It’s not going to be that simple. So it would still be shocking when he actually does die. I’m counting on people being cynical about it. LORRE : I’m counting on people laughing. PRADY : The answer to a lot of questions is because it made us laugh, and we hope it makes other people laugh. DEADLINE: Some of the spoilers are really mild, but this one was like, first: who’s Gary?, and then it was that simple, he just died. PRADY : He died, didn’t he? And he really just died. PENN : Yeah, it’s just totally pointless. LORRE : “Follow me.” PRADY: “Follow me.” Oh. Musical Variations The Simpsons theme composer Elfman recalled “the crazy thing” that happened after he was asked to write main title music for Stuart Fails To Save the Universe and, as a Big Bang fan, agreed to do it. “I wrote it, Chuck loved it, and he said, ‘So here’s the thing. I need you to do 10 variations on it,'” Elfman said. “I thought about it for two seconds. No one’d ever asked me to do that before but I just said, ‘You got it.'” And he did it, drawing inspiration from the particular episode for its unique theme music. “It wasn’t even difficult,” he said. “Each episode, just mix it up and try things. The news brings to an end a ten-year run at the super-indie, during which time he executive-produced shows such as Picnic at Hanging Rock and films including Bugonia and Pillion . Vesper has joined Fremantle from AMC Networks in 2016, after a five-year period at the cable network. At Fremantle, he was a key player in the company’s switch from a largely unscripted producer to one also a player in scripted. During his tenure, Fremantle released 80 films and is on track to release its hundredth this year. Related Stories Casting Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation 'You Are Here' For BBC & Starz Cancellations and Renewals 'American Idol' Renewed For Season 25 At ABC He was based in London and reported to Fremantle Group COO and CEO for Continental Europe Andrea Scrosati, who will lead the film and drama teams on an interim basis alongside the wider management teams at those units. Watch on Deadline “With Christian at the helm, we have established our drama and film business and delivered both consistent success and critical acclaim,” said Scrosati. “Our scripted portfolio is today a key component of our business and recognised across the industry. Christian is a creative at heart, and his vision has helped build the credibility of our drama and film slate. We appreciate that he now wishes to focus on new horizons, and we all wish him well in the future.” “After ten years with Fremantle, I have decided that the time is right to step down from my role as CEO Film and Drama,” added Vesper. “I would like to thank Jennifer Mullin and Andrea Scrosati for their incredible support, ambition and creative spirit, enabling us to build our film and drama capabilities. I am extremely proud of what we have achieved together, and the fact we will deliver our 100th film this year underlines the progress made.” Under Vesper’s leadership, Fremantle struck scripted partnerships with Emma Stone and Dave McCary’s Fruit Tree Productions; Kristen Stewart, Dylan Meyer and Maggie McLean’s Nevermind Pictures; Pablo and Juan de Dios Larraín’s Fabula; Rachel Weisz and Polly Stokes’ Astral Projection; Edward Berger’s Nine Hours; Johan Renck and Michael Parets’ Sinestra Films; Sarah Condon’s Fair Harbour; and Richard Yee and Krishnendu Majumdar’s Me+You Productions. Vesper was also exec producer on the Oscar-nominated Emma Stone and Jesse Plemons starrer Bugonia , Cannes prize winner Pillion , Daniel Craig pic Queer , Maria , Australian series Picnic at Hanging Rock and BBC/TVNZ miniseries The Luminaries . More recently, he worked to set up Fox’s Baywatch rival. Elsewhere, he worked with Angelina Jolie on Without Blood , Joe Wright on Sky Italia’s M. Son of the Century and Tom Alfredsson on Faithless . Prior to Fremantle, he had a 14-year spell at Sundance TV, the AMC Networks channel. There he worked on Rectify , The Honorable Woman , The Last Panthers , Top of the Lake and Deutschland 83 . He also had roles at HBO, iFilm, October Films and USA Films.
